asset.description: The registry stablecoin priced, as CODE.issuer (40-hex code)

figure.description: The book statistic of the direct pair, in its base: spread_bps, spread / mid in basis points; depth_bid_k and depth_ask_k, the funded base quantity of the bids or asks priced within k bps of mid, bounds included; its live value is the same statistic of this request's book, spread_bps not rounded to 2 decimals

window.description: The baseline window: the 672 15-minute slots (7 days) up to the current one

baseline.description: The 7-day stored baseline of the book of the metric's direct pair, in the metric's base and quote order; null while every figure warms up, when no stored series tracks the pair, or when the stored series cannot be read or lacks a figure

depth_at_peg_50.description: Funded quantity of asset on both sides of the direct book priced within 50 bps of expected, bounds included; null without expected

reasons.description: At most one baseline reason: warming_up while a baseline figure has fewer than 288 stored slots; not_tracked when no stored series tracks the pair; baseline_unavailable when the stored series cannot be read or lacks a figure; empty otherwise

anyOf.description: ECB reference of an EUR asset; null for a USD asset or without a stored ECB rate

age_days.description: Whole UTC days from rate_date to the answer's date

rate_date.description: Date of the stored ECB rate (YYYY-MM-DD)

source.description: Attribution of the rate: "Source: ECB statistics"

usd_per_eur.description: Stored ECB reference rate, USD per EUR, unmodified

routes.description: The available routes only, in the order clob_direct, amm_direct, via_xrp

deviation_bps.description: Deviation of observed from expected in basis points, rounded half-up to 2 decimals; null when expected is null

observed.description: Price of asset in against on this route

route.description: clob_direct: mid of the direct book; amm_direct: fee-free spot of the direct pool; via_xrp: mid of XRP in against over mid of XRP in asset

status.description: Band of the headline deviation, a defined computation and not advice; unknown without a route

description: How far a registry stablecoin trades from its peg on the XRP Ledger DEX: the deviation of each price route, their median and a status. When to use: To check, from the XRP Ledger's own order books and AMM pools, how far a registry stablecoin trades from its peg against another registry coin, and how much funded depth sits near the peg. Prefer another tool: To check that an issued currency is the canonical registry coin, or to read its issuer posture (use `/v1/xrpl/stablecoin/{asset}`); for an asset outside the registry, which this route refuses, read its order book (`/v1/xrpl/orderbook`) or its AMM pool (`/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`). Example: xrpl_metrics_peg {"asset":"524C555344000000000000000000000000000000.rMxCKbEDwqr76QuheSUMdEGf4B9xJ8m5De"} Paid: 0.04356 USDC or 0.0363 EURC per call on Solana mainnet, VAT included. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.03 EUR-denominated units (approx 33 calls per bundle) or 0.036 USD-denominated units (approx 22 calls per bundle).

against.description: USD stablecoin of the registry, other than asset, it is priced in; omit for the peg default (the other USD registry coin for a USD asset, RLUSD for an EUR asset): `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

asset.description: XRPL stablecoin of the registry whose peg is measured, by its canonical code and issuer: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.
